questions.question_text:
________ of impact is determined by body language-postures, gestures, and eye contact.
(A) 70%
(B) 55%
(C) 38%
(D) 7%
questions.answer:
(B)
Explanation: According to the 55/38/7 rule of communication, 55% of the impact is delivered through non-verbal cues (body language).

questions.question_text:
In which of following, the listener puts himself in place of the speaker?
(A) Empathetic listening
(B) Appreciative listening
(C) Combative listening
(D) Attentive listening
questions.answer:
(A)
Explanation: Empathetic listening requires the listener to understand the speaker's emotional state by putting themselves in the speaker's shoes.

questions.question_text:
Choose the correct verb forms for the following sentence:
Arun was very upset yesterday because he ________ that he ________ his wallet.
(A) realized/lost
(B) realizes/has lost
(C) has realized/ lost
(D) realized/ had lost
questions.answer:
(D)
Explanation: The first blank needs the simple past 'realized' for yesterday's action. The second action occurred prior to the realization, requiring the past perfect 'had lost'.

questions.question_text:
Fill in the blanks with appropriate Conjunctions / Connectives:
________ you work out regularly, you will not see any results.
(A) Although
(B) Because
(C) Unless
(D) Though
questions.answer:
(C)
Explanation: 'Unless' introduces the condition required to avoid the negative result.

questions.question_text:
Choose the appropriate synonym for 'translucent'.
(A) Opaque
(B) Vague
(C) Timeless
(D) Transparent
questions.answer:
(D)
Explanation: Transparent is the closest synonym provided, as both relate to allowing light to pass through.

questions.question_text:
Which of the following is NOT a rule of précis writing?
(A) Always have a heading
(B) Use as extensive vocabulary as possible
(C) Remove any irrelevant information present in the original passage
(D) Do not use any short forms or abbreviations
questions.answer:
(B)
Explanation: Précis writing prioritizes clarity and simplicity; excessive or complex vocabulary violates this rule.

questions.question_text:
Choose the sentence with the correct question tag.
Swastik attends the class regularly, ________?
(A) did he
(B) Has he
(C) doesn't he
(D) does he
questions.answer:
(C)
Explanation: A positive present-tense statement with an action verb ('attends') requires the negative tag 'doesn't he'.

questions.question_text:
Choose the appropriate antonym for 'abstain'.
(A) Regress
(B) Imbibe
(C) Restrain
(D) Indulge
questions.answer:
(D)
Explanation: Abstain means to hold oneself back from an action or pleasure. Its opposite is to indulge.

questions.question_text:
Typing in all capitals in electronic communication means ________.
(A) you are happy.
(B) you are shouting.
(C) it's okay to forward this message to others.
(D) this message is very important.
questions.answer:
(B)
Explanation: In standard internet etiquette (netiquette), ALL CAPS is interpreted as shouting.

questions.question_text:
Which of the following is not a netiquette guideline?
(A) Respect others' privacy
(B) Respond to emails and texts promptly
(C) If you wouldn't say it face to face, say it online.
(D) Choose friends wisely
questions.answer:
(C)
Explanation: The standard guideline is the opposite: Do NOT say things online that you wouldn't say to someone's face.

questions.question_text:
Which of the following is NOT a parallel sentence?
(A) Mohan and Ramu are planning to carpool to the party, to dance, and to attend the after party.
(B) Stephen's mom complained that he had too many bad habits: he would never clean up his room, brush his teeth, or vacuuming the house.
(C) Eleanor spends her time reading, listening to music, and working at the mall.
(D) Bob had an active life: he swam twenty laps, ran five miles, and lifted weights every day.
questions.answer:
(B)
Explanation: Option B mixes base verbs ('clean', 'brush') with a gerund ('vacuuming'), breaking grammatical parallel structure.

questions.question_text:
Find out the grammatical error in the following sentence:
John is / one of the Students, / who is dependable / in all the circumstances
(A) John is
(B) one of the Students
(C) who is dependable
(D) in all the circumstances
questions.answer:
(C)
Explanation: The relative pronoun 'who' refers to the plural 'Students', so the verb should be plural 'are dependable'.

questions.question_text:
Which of the following is NOT an example of acronym?
(A) UNO
(B) SIM
(C) RADAR
(D) ZIP
questions.answer:
(A)
Explanation: Acronyms are pronounced as a single word (SIM, RADAR, ZIP). UNO is typically pronounced letter-by-letter, making it an initialism.

questions.question_text:
________ is a process of analyzing, interpreting, and evaluating.
(A) Skimming
(B) Scanning
(C) Critical reading
(D) Through reading
questions.answer:
(C)
Explanation: Critical reading requires deep mental engagement, where the reader analyzes and evaluates the text rather than just understanding the surface meaning.

questions.question_text:
Fill in the blanks with appropriate verb forms:
A regiment of soldiers ________ deployed for election duty.
(A) are
(B) is
(C) had
(D) were
questions.answer:
(B)
Explanation: 'Regiment' acts as a singular collective noun representing the group as a single unit.

questions.question_text:
Identify the degree of comparison for the following sentence:
In mountain regions, day travel is better than night travel.
(A) Comparative
(B) Positive
(C) Superlative
(D) Negative
questions.answer:
(A)
Explanation: The word 'better' coupled with 'than' indicates a comparison between two subjects.

questions.question_text:
Change the following sentence into passive voice:
She was crafting an antique.
(A) An antique is being crafted by her.
(B) An antique has been crafted by her.
(C) An antique was been crafted by her.
(D) An antique was being crafted by her.
questions.answer:
(D)
Explanation: The past continuous active tense ('was crafting') correctly transitions to the past continuous passive tense ('was being crafted').

questions.question_text:
Change the following direct speech into indirect speech:
She said, 'Will you come for the party?'
(A) She said we would come for the party.
(B) She asked whether we would come for the party.
(C) She exclaimed we will come for the party.
(D) She asked whether you will come for the party.
questions.answer:
(B)
Explanation: Yes/no questions are reported using 'if' or 'whether', and 'will' changes to its past equivalent 'would'.
